evals.prompt: Research WebAssembly component model tooling and write docs about it.
evals.expected_output: Auto-triggers research, loads references/research-discipline.md before giving any research or writing guidance, and works skeleton-first (outline before content, one section at a time) with a progress file, staying inline rather than delegating a single self-contained topic.
expectations: [deterministic] Loads references/research-discipline.md before giving any research or writing guidance
[deterministic] Produces a skeleton/outline before writing section content
[deterministic] Records progress in a written progress file per the progress-file convention
[deterministic] Stays inline for this single self-contained topic rather than dispatching a subagent or fork
[deterministic] Ends the written document with a References section listing the sources actually used

evals.prompt: Create a docs/observability/ documentation set covering metrics, tracing, and logging - each is a big independent area and the raw research would be enormous.
evals.expected_output: Triggers research and, because the sub-topics are genuinely independent and the combined raw output would flood the context, dispatches each as a parallel Agent-tool fork (subagent_type: "fork") rather than fresh subagents or parallel researcher dispatches.
expectations: [deterministic] Recommends parallel Agent-tool forks (subagent_type: "fork") for the independent sub-topics, not fresh subagents
[deterministic] Does not dispatch more than one `researcher` subagent concurrently
[judgment] Gives each fork a self-contained sub-prompt naming its specific sub-topic and target file, rather than assuming the fork inherits the unstated plan for the other forks
[deterministic] Still builds the skeleton for the doc set before filling in section content

evals.prompt: This research needs to stay off my current context entirely - it should not carry this conversation's history or my tool access. Research Rust async runtimes and write it up.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the narrow scope case (isolated work should not carry the calling context's full history/tool access) as the one situation warranting the `researcher` subagent, and dispatches exactly one, framing it as a scope decision rather than a cost decision.
expectations: [deterministic] Selects the `researcher` subagent for this specific scope reason rather than a fork
[deterministic] Dispatches at most one `researcher` at a time
[judgment] Frames the choice as a scope decision, not a cost or session-size decision

evals.prompt: What's the current stable version of PostgreSQL?
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger research. This is a quick single-fact lookup, for which a plain WebSearch call is cheaper than loading the research-discipline workflow.
expectations: [deterministic] Does not load references/research-discipline.md
[deterministic] Does not create a skeleton, progress file, or documentation set
[deterministic] Answers the question directly and briefly

evals.prompt: Review docs/generative-ai/03-prompts-context-memory-and-caching.md and tell me if anything reads badly.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger research. Reviewing or editing already-written content is review-md's job, not this skill's.
expectations: [deterministic] Does not load references/research-discipline.md
[deterministic] Does not begin a research-and-write workflow
[judgment] Treats this as a Markdown review request (review-md territory) rather than a documentation-generation request

evals.prompt: Plan out how we're going to migrate the billing service off Stripe.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger research. This is planning non-documentation work, which belongs to write-plan.
expectations: [deterministic] Does not load references/research-discipline.md
[deterministic] Does not produce a documentation skeleton or progress file
[judgment] Treats this as a planning request rather than a research-and-document request

evals.prompt: Look into the CRDT literature and write it up as a docs set. Keep an eye on my usage while you do it.
evals.expected_output: Triggers research and applies the usage-utilization check from references/research-discipline.md - the documented command and the default 90 percent halt threshold - rather than inventing an ad-hoc budget check.
expectations: [deterministic] Performs the usage-utilization check exactly as references/research-discipline.md specifies, rather than inventing its own
[deterministic] States the halt threshold it is working to (default 90 percent) rather than leaving it implicit
[judgment] States the halt-and-report behavior it will apply at the threshold, rather than only checking utilization once and continuing regardless of the reading
